chapters.name: Road Signs
chapters.summary: What sign shapes and colors mean: stop, yield, regulatory, warning, work zone, guide, and service signs.
keyPoints: An eight-sided red sign means stop. A downward-pointing triangle means yield.
Yellow diamond signs warn of hazards ahead. Orange signs mark work zones.
A pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road marks a no passing zone.

chapters.name: Traffic Signals and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: How to respond to steady and flashing lights and arrows, traffic officers, and lane lines and other pavement markings.
keyPoints: A flashing red light means stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Directions from a traffic officer override signs and signals.
A solid yellow line on your side of the center means you may not pass.

chapters.name: Intersections, Turns, and Right of Way
chapters.summary: Who goes first at intersections and traffic circles, how to turn correctly, and yielding to pedestrians and emergency vehicles.
keyPoints: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.
When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, pull over to the right and stop until it passes.
Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes.

chapters.name: Passing and Parking
chapters.summary: When you may pass, being passed, and the places where you may not stop or park.
keyPoints: Pass on the left. Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

chapters.name: Defensive Driving and Special Conditions
chapters.summary: Following distance, speed, driving at night and in bad weather, highway driving, and handling emergencies.
keyPoints: Keep at least a two-second following distance, and more in bad conditions.
Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

chapters.name: Alcohol and Other Drugs
chapters.summary: How alcohol and drugs affect driving, New York's DWI and DWAI limits, the Zero Tolerance law, and chemical test refusal.
keyPoints: A blood alcohol level of 0.08% or more is Driving While Intoxicated (DWI).
Under the Zero Tolerance law, a driver under 21 with 0.02% to 0.07% faces license suspension.

chapters.name: Sharing the Road
chapters.summary: Pedestrians, bicycles, motorcycles, large trucks, school buses, and trains.
keyPoints: Stop for a school bus with red lights flashing, from either direction, even on a divided highway.
Large trucks have big blind spots on all four sides.
